item.title: Brandon King's 81 not out guides West Indies to 1-0 series lead against Bangladesh
item.description: West Indies defeated Bangladesh by eight wickets in the first Test after chasing down a target of 170 runs on Saturday. Opener Brandon King led the charge with an unbeaten 81 off 115 balls, hitting 10 fours and a six. Kavem Hodge supported him with an unbeaten 31 as West Indies comfortably secured a 1-0 lead in the two-match series. West Indies' spinners played a major role in the win, bowling Bangladesh out for just 142 in their second innings. Captain Roston Chase picked up five wickets for 36 runs, while Jomel Warrican claimed four for 63. Warrican had also taken five wickets in Bangladesh's first innings. Bangladesh resumed Day 4 at 79 for six but managed only 63 more runs. Nayeem Hasan top-scored with 52, recording his maiden Test half-century, but Chase eventually dismissed him to complete his five-wicket haul. King and Campbell lead the chase Chasing 170 on a difficult pitch, West Indies openers Brandon King and John Campbell chose to attack rather than defend against Bangladesh's spinners. The pair added 112 runs for the first wicket, putting their team in a strong position. King brought up his sixth Test half-century, while Campbell scored 49 after making 54 in the first innings. Shoriful Islam dismissed Campbell with a swinging delivery, while Hasan Mahmud removed Tagenarine Chanderpaul for one. However, Bangladesh could not create further pressure as King and Hodge added an unbeaten 50-run partnership to finish the chaseEarlier, Bangladesh scored 272 in their first innings before West Indies replied with 245. The second Test will be played in Sylhet next week, with Bangladesh looking to level the series.

item.title: Returning Estevao brings X-factor to strikerless Chelsea
item.description: Estevao had two goals ruled out for offside against Manchester United [Getty Images] Estevao Willian had not started a Premier League match this season before his electric display against Manchester United on Saturday. The 19-year-old winger was an unused substitute for the midweek penalty shootout defeat by Liverpool but was still serenaded with chants from away fans at Anfield. Three days later, after questions had been raised about the Brazil international's lack of opportunities, Chelsea supporters made their feelings clear. Early on against United at Stamford Bridge, supporters chanted "Steve-o", their tongue-in-cheek nickname for the £38m signing from Palmeiras. This time he was on the field, making things happen in a team that lacked a recognised striker, and the loud backing from the stands appeared justified. Estevao had an early goal ruled out for offside before another fine near-post finish in the second half was disallowed - a marginal decision. At the end of his 86-minute display in the Blues' 2-0 victory, Estevao received a standing ovation from the home crowd and a hug from Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso. He had six shots, the joint-most by a Chelsea player in a Premier League match this season, along with a host of other impressive attacking contributions. He recorded 12 touches in the opposition penalty area, created three chances, delivered eight crosses and completed five dribbles - all either the most or joint-most by a Chelsea player in Saturday's match. Estevao's limited recent involvement remains curious. Before this, he had made only one start this season, against League One side Luton Town in the Carabao Cup in September. It has led to speculation in the Brazilian media that he is unhappy or pushing for a move. However, both publicly and privately, sources at Chelsea and those close to Estevao have suggested no signs of discontent. There has been widespread praise for his professionalism behind the scenes and a feeling that he has been unfortunate, not least with the form of Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro, which has limited his opportunities. Chelsea's tendency to score first or take early leads has also meant more defensive options have often been chosen from the bench. There was talk before Saturday's match that Alonso was keeping his plans to start Estevao against Manchester United under wraps, having faced questions from the media about the winger in the build-up. He confirmed after the victory that the decision had already been made. In fact, it was made in the aftermath of last weekend's home defeat by Tottenham. "We spoke after Tottenham and he knew that he was going to be playing tonight, today," Alonso said. "He has had the best response to show that he deserves more, that he was prepared, and that's what you want from a football player, so I'm very happy for him. "He deserved to enjoy his game. item.title: Martinez's 'inexplicable' 83 seconds cost Man Utd and Carrick
item.description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez is shown a red card by referee Peter Bankes during the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea [Getty Images] Lisandro Martinez made his way to the tunnel slowly and silently. The whistles and jeers of the Chelsea fans were ringing in his ears. Manchester United coach Jonny Evans had a brief word, but Martinez didn't pay any attention. As a player, Martinez has scaled the heights. Part of the Argentina squad that won the World Cup in 2022 and reached the final last summer. But at Stamford Bridge, when Michael Carrick needed his side to step up and his senior players to set an example, Martinez did the very opposite. Eighteen days after Martinez called out United's summer recruitment, he suffered the kind of meltdown that would have left most United fans questioning whether that poor recruitment involved not turfing the 28-year-old out of Old Trafford. The former Ajax defender had been part of a much improved United performance at Stamford Bridge and Carrick's team should have been ahead at half-time. Even when Morgan Rogers gave Chelsea a second-half lead, they had done enough for the visiting fans to believe a comeback was possible. Instead, in the space one minute and 23 seconds, Martinez committed two fouls that left Carrick's side 2-0 down and playing with 10 men - with Chelsea subsequently cruising to victory . However this woeful period unfolds, it is unlikely Martinez's recklessness will be forgotten. Martinez 'rightly sent off' Martinez was sent off with 27 minutes of normal time remaining [Getty Images] It was noticeable that Carrick did not look at Martinez as he made his way off the pitch. He was more concentrated on trying to come up with a plan with his assistant Steve Holland to get through the rest of the game. Asked afterwards if he felt let down by Martinez, Carrick said he had not had a chance to view the incident again. "I've not seen it back, so I don't know if it was or not" adding "it's a big moment in the game". Carrick continued: "The second goal and losing a man at that stage had a big influence on it, for sure." For context, Martinez, already on a booking, chose the moment Estevao swung over the corner to try and block off Wesley Fofana at the far post. In the process, Martinez raised his elbow and caught the defender in the face. The incident was missed in real time but video assistant referee (VAR) James Bell advised referee Peter Bankes to go to the screen and the obvious conclusion was reached. World Cup final official Darren Cann called Martinez's actions "inexplicable". "He jumped into him, making no attempt to play the ball and not even looking at the ball as it came in from the corner," Cann told BBC Sport. "Martinez was rightly sent off for two bookable offences, as well as conceding a needless penalty for the reckless challenge on Fofana." item.title: Robyn Choi’s Surge Makes Her A Genuine LPGA Title Threat
item.description: May 31, 2018; Shoal Creek, AL, USA; Robyn Choi putts on the second green during the first round of the U.S. Women's Open Championship golf tournament at Shoal Creek. Mandatory Credit: John David Mercer-USA TODAY Sports Robyn Choi is finally within striking distance of a long-awaited LPGA Tour title, and the path looks clearer than it has in years. The Australian fired a six-under-par 66 on Saturday to sit tied for fourth place at the Maybank Championship in Malaysia. She trails the leader by just four shots, a margin that feels manageable on a course where scores are dropping fast. This isn’t just a good round; it is a genuine shot at her maiden victory. Choi’s round included eight birdies, a display of aggression that has been missing from her game for too long. According to Australian Golf Digest , she has managed only two top-10 results since her rookie season in 2019. That drought ends this weekend if she can keep her foot on the gas. The field is tough, but the gap is small enough to close with a few more hot holes. The Japanese Dominance Choi faces a massive hurdle in defending champion Miyu Yamashita. The Japanese star shot a 67 on Saturday to reach 18 under and hold a two-shot lead. Yamashita is the 2025 Women’s British Open winner and is hunting back-to-back wins in Kuala Lumpur. Australian Golf Digest noted she remains on track for consecutive triumphs, which adds serious pressure to the field. Beating a player on a hot streak is hard, but Choi has the numbers to make it happen. The Japanese presence is strong all around. Yuri Yoshida won last week in South Korea, marking the fourth win for a Japanese player this season. That momentum shifts the odds, but it does not seal the deal. Choi is right there, tied with Thai amateur Marisa Tojai, who also shot a 65. The competition is fierce, but the door is open. Aussie Contingent and the Cut Choi is not the only Australian making waves. Karis Davidson sits tied for 18th at nine under after a 70, while Cassie Porter is a shot further back. Hannah Green posted a 66 to climb to five under. According to the report, these players are all still in the hunt, but Choi has the clear momentum. The pressure is on to convert this chance into a win. A 63, the round of the day, put China’s Yan Liu in a tie for second place. That score includes an eagle and nine birdies, showing just how low the bar is set. If Choi can match that kind of scoring, she will be in the mix on Sunday. The leaderboard is tight, and every shot counts . The next round will define the tournament. The LPGA’s Asian swing is set to end next week with the Toto Japan Classic.

item.title: Füllkrug extends scoring streak as Bremen climb to fifth after beating Hoffenheim
item.description: Füllkrug extends scoring streak as Bremen climb to fifth after beating Hoffenheim Second-half goals from returnees Niclas Füllkrug and Eren Dinkci secured a home win for Werder Bremen against TSG Hoffenheim. With their first back-to-back victory, the hosts climbed to fifth in the standings. Daniel Thioune had to make an early substitution as Mitchell Weiser suffered another setback after making his return from a long-term injury. To no one's surprise, Niclas Füllkrug had Bremen's first real chance before Marco Grüll's header narrowly missed the target. Hoffenheim's best chance of the first-half came in the 45th minute when Amos Pieper cleared Adam Hložek's header from the goal line. The Czechia international was also instrumental in Hoffenheim's first chance after the break, but Youri Regeer denied Fisnik Asllani. Füllkrug started the second-half strongly as Oliver Baumann had to make a decent save from his powerful effort minutes before he got his customary goal. The 33-year-old striker won a physical tussle against Hoffenheim's defense before firing an unstoppable shot for his ninth goal of the season. Asllani had a couple of half chances to bring back Hoffenheim into the game, but Bremen dominated the proceedings after their goal. And Eren Dinkci sealed the win for the hosts eight minutes from time with a composed finish after Grüll's league-high sixth assist of the season. Bremen rose to fifth place after winning back-to-back games in Bundesliga for the first time this season. Füllkrug extended his scoring run to eight games in all competitions. Meanwhile, Hoffenheim suffered back-to-back defeats in the cup and Bundesliga.

item.description: The Green Bay Packers are 5-3 on the season following their 27-19 victory over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football. While they remain out of first place in the NFC North, they are at least keeping pace with the rest of the division and are currently a part of the convoluted playoff picture. For much of the year so far, it has been Green Bay’s defense that has shone the brightest. Playing without star pass rusher Micah Parsons, who is expected to return in Week 12 on Thanksgiving, the Packers defensive unit leads the NFL in both sacks and takeaways (as of this writing). What many outside of Green Bay are now starting to realize after watching their latest Prime Time game is that Jordan Love , too, is a huge reason for the Packers success up to this point in the season. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love should be an MVP candidate Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) looks to pass during the first quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images While the rest of the NFL has yet to play their Week Eight games, a look at Love’s numbers so far in 2026 are indications that he will end up among the league leaders in the most important offensive categories by the end of the season. Currently, Love leads the league in passing yards (2,246), passing touchdowns (16), attempts (312), and completions (196). His 61.5% completion percentage looks, well, less than ideal. However, it should be noted that his pass catchers lead the league in drops with 18. Matthew Golden, who is otherwise having a stellar season, leads the NFL with eight. If just half of those team drops had been caught, Love’s completion percentage would be 64.8%. If they were all caught, it would be 67.7%, which would rank among the top-ten in the league. In addition to the woeful drops by his receivers, Love has had the worst protection in the league. Green Bay’s offensive line is giving him just 2.48 seconds to throw, which ranks 35th among quarterbacks who have played in the NFL this season. Of course, the line’s woes are not limited to pass protection. The Packers run game ranks last in the league with 60.6 yards per game, meaning that Love shoulders the burden of virtually the entire offense. Through eight games, Love has accounted for 82% of Green Bay’s yards gained on offense in 2026. The defense has definitely helped the Packers win games, but the fact of the matter is that any lesser quarterback would not be able to produce on the level that Love is. His production should get him some MVP consideration by season’s end, but whether or not the Packers’ overall performance will get the attention of voters remains to be seen. If he is able to lead Green Bay back to the postseason despite all of the other struggles on offense, he should be the unquestioned MVP of the league. item.title: ‘If that were to happen…’: LeBron James’ potential statue for Lakers receives verdicts from Magic Johnson’s ex-teammate
item.description: Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images Five-time NBA champion Michael Cooper has stated that LeBron James deserves a statue outside Crypto.com Arena as his legendary stint with the Purple and Gold came to an end this offseason. Having left the team with one NBA championship and several major NBA records, including the all-time scoring record, which he broke in 2023 by surpassing another Laker great, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, James definitely had some great moments as a Laker. He was with the team for eight seasons, and although after the championship, there wasn’t much success, King James was committed to the team until his last game. As the icon that he is, there is an expectation among his fans that the Lakers will not only retire his jersey but also build him a statue outside the arena. Michael Cooper explains why LeBron James deserves a statue The Lakers are the third team James has represented in the NBA. However, it is the longest he has ever played for a franchise. While his achievements in Purple and Gold do not compare to the likes of Shaquille O’Neal, Kobe Bryant and Magic Johnson, Cooper believes the King has done enough to be honoured with a statue. “Well, I think that’s going to take time if that were to happen, but anybody that has won a championship in Los Angeles for the Lakers and the player that LeBron James is, deserves a statue out there,” Cooper said in an interview with Brandon “Scoop B” Robinson. Kendrick Perkins also seemed to agree that the four-time champion deserved to be honoured with a statue. In his eight seasons with the team, James averaged 25.9 points, 7.9 assists and 7.7 rebounds. He also made eight All-Star teams and seven All-NBA appearances, showcasing brilliance throughout his stint in LA. Although fans would have liked the player to deliver a few more championships, injuries and roster depth always seemed to hold the team back. While James getting a statue may be something that divides opinions among Lakers fans, Cooper believes that the King definitely deserves to have his jersey retired. “Well, I think when he retires, yeah. LeBron’s going to be… like a lot of people, Wilt Chamberlain’s jersey is retired in different places—Philadelphia and Los Angeles. So, of course. Bron won a championship, so you have to honor him like that,” Cooper said. James’ first game back in LA is set for Christmas Day. It will be interesting to see the kind of reception he gets from Lakers fans. He has been extremely positive about his time in LA, but with fans having mixed reactions to his exit, this is definitely one of the most anticipated Christmas Day games. item.title: Demirovic at the double as Stuttgart see off Leverkusen
item.description: Demirovic at the double as Stuttgart see off Leverkusen Bayer Leverkusen dropped points at the BayArena for the first time this season in the Bundesliga on Saturday, losing 2-4 to VfB Stuttgart, who claimed three much-needed points. The visitors took the lead in the 14th minute, with Ermedin Demirovic firing home the rebound after Mark Flekken had rushed off his line to push the ball away from Bilal El Khannouss. Stuttgart doubled their lead just eight minutes later, as Jamie Leweling pounced on another rebound following a corner. Leverkusen responded in the 28th minute, however, with Patrik Schick heading home from a corner after Dennis Seimen failed to keep out his effort. Both sides came close to adding to the scoreline before half-time, but the crossbar denied Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza before keeping out Leweling's attempt to grab his second goal of the afternoon. Early in the second half, Stuttgart restored their two-goal lead when El Khannouss unleashed an unstoppable low shot from the edge of the area to put the visitors 3-1 up. Diego Moreira, one of Leverkusen's livelier players in the second half, tried to bring his team back into the game with a fierce shot in the 56th minute, but Seimen denied him with a good save. Instead, Stuttgart went 4-1 up in the 65th minute, as Deniz Undav sent in an inch-perfect pass behind the Leverkusen defence to pick out Ermedin Demirovic, who scored his second goal of the game. Leverkusen refused to give up, though, and Ibrahim Maza gave them a glimmer of hope when he headed in Gutierrez's cross in the 79th minute to make it 2-4. But it wasn't enough for Leverkusen, who suffered their third consecutive defeat against Stuttgart. Sebastian Hoeneß's men will be pleased with the win, which sees them take a big step away from the relegation zone after a disappointing start to the season.
